description: Model file format matrix for LLM engines. Describes each format's quantization support, GPU memory layout, and porting implications.

gguf.name: GGUF (GGML Universal Format)
gguf.description: Single-file binary format with model weights, metadata, and quantization info. Used by Maya for both GLM and DS4 packs.

quant_types.bf16: BF16 — hardware-supported on CDNA2, SM_89, Arc; emulated elsewhere
quant_types.q4_1: 4-bit quantized (GGML Q4_1) — 4.5 bits/weight, with sign + scale
quant_types.q5_1: 5-bit quantized (GGML Q5_1) — 5.5 bits/weight, with sign + scale
quant_types.exl3_2.9: 3-bit EXL3 with grouped matrix quantization — 2.9 bits/weight

porting_notes.AMD: EXL3 kernels on gfx1030 use older v_dot4_i32_i8 (hip_compat/intrinsics.hpp). gfx1201+ supports newer packed dot4. No tensor cores — use F32 fallback for bf16.
porting_notes.NVIDIA: EXL3 uses tensor cores on sm_80+. Q8_0 uses imad instruction. All quantized dequant on CPU for non-native formats.
porting_notes.Intel: EXL3 via DPAS on Arc. Q8_0 via DP4a.

safetensors.name: SafeTensors
safetensors.description: Safe tensor format — no arbitrary code execution, header-only metadata + raw weight bytes. Used by HF transformers.

gpu_kernels.loading: Memory-mapped — direct mmap, no dequant at load time
gpu_kernels.compute: Depends on framework (torch → Triton kernels, JAX → XLA)

porting_notes.AMD: No native bitsandbytes support. Use rocm-torch or custom kernels. GPTQ kernels often CUDA-only.
porting_notes.NVIDIA: Full ecosystem — bitsandbytes, auto-gptq, GPTQ-for-LLaMa all support CUDA.
porting_notes.Intel: Use intel-extension-for-transformers, or convert to GGUF.

huggingface_hub.name: HuggingFace Hub (sharded)
huggingface_hub.description: PyTorch checkpoint shards. Can be .bin (pickle, unsafe) or .safetensors.
huggingface_hub.porting_notes: For porting to C++ engines: convert to GGUF first (see tools/iq_pack.py). Direct .bin parsing requires custom PyTorch-free loader.

onnx.name: ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange)
onnx.description: Intermediate representation for AI models. Hardware-agnostic graph + weights.

gpu_kernels.runtime: ONNX Runtime with CUDA/Metal/Vulkan/DirectML execution provider
gpu_kernels.compute: ORT handles kernel dispatch — no custom kernels needed
gpu_kernels.quant: ORT quantization tools produce Q4/Q8 weight-only quant

onnx.porting_notes: ORT can target many backends (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, DirectML). For custom GPU kernels, need to extract ONNX weights and write custom runtime.

hdf5.name: HDF5 (TensorFlow checkpoint format)
hdf5.description: Hierarchical Data Format v5. Used by Keras/TF model.save().
hdf5.porting_notes: Rarely used for LLMs. Convert to safetensors or GGUF for GPU inference.

mlc_llm.name: MLC LLM format (GGUF-compatible)
mlc_llm.description: MLC's format is GGUF with their own quantization (R4F4, etc.).
mlc_llm.porting_notes: Compatible with GGUF tooling. MLC's webgpu backend targets Vulkan/Metal/DirectX.

to_gguf.from_safetensors: tools/iq_pack.py (Maya's native pack) — reads HF safetensors, writes GGUF with BF16 preserves
to_gguf.from_huggingface: tools/iq_pack.py + gguf-py — exports tokenizer + chat template too
to_gguf.from_pytorch_bin: tools/iq_pack.py — converts .bin shards to GGUF via gguf-py
to_gguf.from_onnx: onnx-to-gguf scripts or convert via safetensors intermediate

from_gguf.to_torch: Not directly — extract weights and load into PyTorch model
from_gguf.to_huggingface: Tools exist (e.g., gguf-to-hf) but require model architecture code
